subject.title: fix: allow trusted host-read html after outbound staging

question: Should OpenClaw accept sha256+size SQLite provenance as the permanent trust mechanism for generated HTML that is staged into media/outbound and later reloaded with host-read enabled?
rationale: The implementation appears fail-closed, but it expands local HTML host-read trust beyond the temp root and stores trust metadata, which automation should not approve on behalf of maintainers.

options.title: Accept Provenance-Gated Trust
options.body: Treat the SQLite provenance row plus same-buffer sha256/size verification as sufficient to carry generated-HTML trust through outbound staging, then merge once normal exact-head gates are satisfied.

options.title: Tighten Lifecycle First
options.body: Require additional lifecycle constraints such as TTL-based row pruning or chunked stale-row deletion before accepting the new stored trust surface.

options.title: Reject Staged HTML Trust
options.body: Keep outbound-staged HTML blocked and rely on PDF or another non-HTML workaround until a different security design is chosen.

recommendation.title: Accept Provenance-Gated Trust
recommendation.body: Treat the SQLite provenance row plus same-buffer sha256/size verification as sufficient to carry generated-HTML trust through outbound staging, then merge once normal exact-head gates are satisfied.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the original trusted generated HTML host-read seam and the SQLite state ownership refactor, so they are the best available owner for accepting or redirecting this boundary.
